headline: Nahid Islam: Sheikh Hasina will return only to face execution
summary: The opposition Chief Whip says the former PM's return depends on diplomatic talks with Delhi and the execution of her death sentence.
details: Nahid Islam, convener of the National Citizens' Party (NCP) and opposition Chief Whip of the National Parliament, stated that former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina will only return to Bangladesh to have her death sentence executed.
Speaking at an event in Dhaka's Kakrail on Friday, he emphasized that the government should use diplomatic and legal channels to bring the 'genocidal' former leader back to the country.

Referring to a recent Reuters interview where Hasina mentioned plans to return in December, Nahid Islam remarked that the country has already suffered 16 years of destruction and her return should only be for the purpose of the execution.
He asserted that the terms of her return—whether she surrenders or how she arrives—will be decided by the Bangladesh government through discussions with Delhi, rather than by Hasina herself.
Nahid Islam further noted that executing the death sentence would be a major step toward national stability and urged the government to act swiftly.
He warned that any attempt to heat up the political situation centered around Sheikh Hasina or the Awami League would be detrimental to the government if tolerated.
The Chief Whip also claimed that the Awami League is not a political party but is controlled by Delhi, meaning Hasina's decisions and statements are permitted by India.
Additionally, he expressed dissatisfaction over the 10-year sentence given to Jasad (Inu) President Hasanul Haq Inu in a crimes against humanity case, questioning the tribunal's judgment.
caption:
Sheikh Hasina will return to Bangladesh only to face the execution of her death sentence, says Chief Whip Nahid Islam.

Nahid Islam, convener of the National Citizens' Party (NCP) and opposition Chief Whip of the National Parliament, stated that former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina will only return to Bangladesh to have her death sentence executed.

Speaking at an event in Dhaka's Kakrail on Friday, he emphasized that the government should use diplomatic and legal channels to bring the 'genocidal' former leader back to the country.

Referring to a recent Reuters interview where Hasina mentioned plans to return in December, Nahid Islam remarked that the country has already suffered 16 years of destruction and her return should only be for the purpose of the execution.

He asserted that the terms of her return—whether she surrenders or how she arrives—will be decided by the Bangladesh government through discussions with Delhi, rather than by Hasina herself.

Nahid Islam further noted that executing the death sentence would be a major step toward national stability and urged the government to act swiftly.

He warned that any attempt to heat up the political situation centered around Sheikh Hasina or the Awami League would be detrimental to the government if tolerated.

The Chief Whip also claimed that the Awami League is not a political party but is controlled by Delhi, meaning Hasina's decisions and statements are permitted by India.

Additionally, he expressed dissatisfaction over the 10-year sentence given to Jasad (Inu) President Hasanul Haq Inu in a crimes against humanity case, questioning the tribunal's judgment.

headline: 11 dead as fast-moving wildfires tear through southern Spain
summary: Foreign nationals, including British citizens, are among the victims of one of the country's worst wildfires in recent years, with 19 people still missing.
details: At least 11 people have been killed in a fast-moving wildfire that tore through a tourist area in Andalusia, southern Spain. Many victims were trapped in burning vehicles or were killed while trying to flee on foot.
Authorities believe many of the deceased are foreign nationals. Four victims, suspected to be British nationals, were found burned to death inside a right-hand drive car.

Around 500 firefighters and the Military Emergency Unit are battling the flames, which have scorched approximately 3,150 hectares of forest and farmland. Around 800 people have been evacuated, including nearly 200 to temporary shelters.

The fire broke out in the Los Gallardos area, specifically affecting the village of Bedar, a popular spot for foreign residents and tourists. Bedar's mayor urged residents to flee their homes as the fire spread rapidly.

Spain is currently experiencing a severe heatwave with temperatures often exceeding 40C, creating tinderbox conditions. Scientists say human-caused climate change is making such extreme weather events more intense.

Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez and King Felipe VI have expressed their grief, with the royal family observing a minute of silence for the victims. Officials warn that conditions could worsen if winds shift.
